poems:
Tuesday resigns. Wednesday takes the desk without a word.
If it isn't Tuesday, the same thing happens anyway.

12:01 a.m.
One minute in and the day already has a record.
A vending machine glowing for no one.
The baby is asleep. Nobody trusts it.
Still open: the gas station, the emergency room, seventeen browser tabs, the question of whether to text him.
12:05. The last bus left at 11:40 and was not sorry about it.
Somewhere a man is eating rice at his desk in the middle of his workday. Here, this.
A cat sits in the sink. The faucet drips into its fur. It stays.
12:08 a.m. is a fine time to remember the thing you said in 2011.
Closing time, n. The forty minutes after the last customer leaves, when the chairs go up and the floor gets what it deserves.
Ice maker. Refrigerator. Somebody's phone charging.

The gamer says one more, meaning four more.
The headset is warm.
His mother went to bed at ten.
12:12 a.m., a number that looks like it means something and does not.
Her side of the closet is still her side of the closet. He has not moved a hanger.
Drink the water. Set the glass where you will knock it over. Do not think about the driveway.
Room 412 wants ice chips. Room 414 wants a different life. The ice chips are achievable.
Streetlight. Wet asphalt. No rain in an hour.
12:17 a.m. The refrigerator kicks on like it has been thinking about it.
Overheard through the wall: no, I said I would call, I did not say when.
New father, hallway, three steps, turn, three steps, turn. He has worn a path in a rug he never liked.
Two headlights, then none.
Last call has happened or is about to. Either way someone orders a round for the table.
You are not going to fix anything at 12:22 a.m., but the mind likes to try the door.

SUBTOTAL 11.40
TIP
TOTAL
SERVER: DANIELLE
CUSTOMER COPY
The dog gets up, circles, lies down facing the other way. This is the whole plan.
Twelve twenty five. The oven light is the only one on, and nobody is baking anything.
A truck downshifting on the bypass.
Somebody's alarm is already set for 4:40. It sits there like a debt.
The last thing on television is a man selling a mattress with great sincerity.
You could go to bed. You have said this before, out loud, to the room.

Half past. The half nobody counts.
The hour is over the way an argument is over.
12:31 a.m. The attendant restocks the roller grill for reasons known only to the roller grill.
A screen door. A porch chair with a towel still on it from whenever.
Night shift lunch, eaten standing, out of the container it came in, at a temperature it did not ask to be.
Someone laughing four apartments away.
Text drafted at 12:35 a.m. Deleted at 12:36. This is the system working.
The plane is over the ocean now. Every shade is down. One person is watching a movie about a wedding.
Take the trash out now, in bare feet, fast, before you think about it.
He is grieving on a schedule that matches nobody's. Twelve thirty eight is his three in the afternoon.
The kettle, cooled. Two mugs. One used.
Twenty minutes to one, which is not a thing anyone says. It is either midnight something or it is late.
The closer counts the drawer twice, not because it was wrong, but because the second count is the quiet part.
In the lost and found: one glove, one vape, a retainer case, a paperback with somebody's boarding pass in it.
12:43 a.m. Nothing is due. Nothing is owed until morning. Enjoy the loophole.
Pipes ticking somewhere behind the wall.
The teenager is awake and has been awake and will say she went to bed at eleven.
A woman in scrubs eats a granola bar in a stairwell because the break room has a television in it.
Second wind, n. A loan. The terms are disclosed at six.
Blue glow on a ceiling. A hand comes up to shade the eyes. Down again.
12:49 a.m. and the phone reports the weather for tomorrow, which is today, which is a lot to take in.
Ten to one. The night has stopped pretending it is an evening.
Down the hall a door closes with the care of someone who does not want a conversation.
Two red lights blinking on a tower.
Nobody wins an argument at 12:53 a.m. The record shows attempts.
The baker's alarm is set. The baker is asleep. These are two separate accomplishments.
Five to. The dishwasher enters its second act, the loud one, the one nobody chose.
Through the floor: I'm not saying that. I'm saying the other thing.
You have three minutes to make this a decision instead of a habit.
One car alarm. Nobody's car.
Twelve fifty nine. The hour ends without being finished. It hands over what it has, which is you, still up.
